journal:
It's the busy days we enjoyed the most, we'd often have to be out before sunrise in the colder months just to move the herd from one pasture to the next. I still don't know how he kept up with it all to be honest, by the time I was old enough to drive the quad out he was pushing on for 12 I think. On the particularly cold mornings he was a lot slower than usual, a long drawn out stretch before hopping in the cargo on the back as we headed out, I could feel his age in those slow movements.

Everytime we got up there i'd be thinking the same thing: "Today he just won't have the energy" or "Maybe I should have brought the younger one to help out" and every time he proved me wrong, he lived for this, and thinking back it was probably the one thing keeping him so carefree and happy. He gave us another five summers before he finally decided to retire.
prompt: Over the shoulder of a young girl sitting on the quadbike with her arm around a border collie, the low evening sun warms both their faces as they stare out at the empty field.

music.why: A girl and her ageing collie watching the low evening sun over a farm field, remembered fondly through his last working years, calls for a warm, looking-back feel with rural acoustic warmth.
